citations.claim: body 0 accelerated to high speed during close approach at first violating step
body 1 accelerated to high speed during close approach at first violating step
initial speed before close approach was much lower, momentum was conserved early

counterfactual.change: reduced dt from 0.017675557924424625 to 0.005 with all else identical (same 9 steps); finer integration removes the momentum drift, showing it is timestep/accuracy dependent at close approach

explanation: Momentum is conserved to machine precision through step 5 (matches step 0), then drifts at step 9 when heavy bodies 0 and 1 close-approach to distance ~1.45 with speeds ~9.2 and ~2.9 and substeps jump to 11. Adaptive substep/leapfrog force evaluation becomes asymmetric or insufficiently accurate under strong acceleration/fast motion, injecting net momentum (and angular momentum). Reducing dt alone removes the failure.
vision_note: The two upper bodies draw closer together from step 6 to step 9 while the distant lower-left body remains nearly stationary. There is no visible explosion, jump, or wall interaction, with motion looking smooth and continuous through step 9.
